approach: Rewrite each always-loaded prompt so it holds the role's job, the output points the schema does not carry, the severity definitions, and every rule a check enforces. Cut text that restates the output schema, the brief (checks, catalog, defaults, READING_RULES) or the contract. Move only explanation and examples (forecast scoring, plan-field examples, verdict-rule rationale, per-severity examples, report contents) into one new optional file, docs/agent-reference.md. Each of the five common frames carries one conditional pointer line. Re-derive the Producer and Verifier budgets from a 90% headroom target in steps of 50, checked against the contract-plus-two-verifier-frames pin by the inequality 0.1·C + K < 0.8·V (C contract, V verifier frame, K largest capability verifier section, all in tokens); when both cannot hold, shrink K or C, or keep V longer, and never trim VERIFIER_FRAME. A new test pins an explicit anchor list (rules and severity terms) in the composed frames and asserts the doc holds none of them. docs/system-facts.md budget lines, two size ratchets in lib.rs, and a CHANGELOG bullet with before and after tokens follow.

decisions.choice: Deliver the reference as an optional on-demand file, docs/agent-reference.md, with a conditional pointer ('if docs/agent-reference.md exists in the working copy'). Move only explanation and examples into it. Every imperative rule, every phrase a test or check pins, and the severity definitions stay in the frames.
decisions.reason: The doc exists only in Athena's own tree, while the frames are compiled in and run on every repository. Compiling a docs/ file in needs edits to xtask/src/main.rs BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS (294-304), eight athena-bin keys in .github/workflows/ci.yml and the nine-glob assertion in xtask/tests/policy.rs (937-940). Those are governance files the brief does not list as deliverables. Optional, non-binding depth means a missing file costs explanation, not correctness. The limit is stated in the doc header and the CHANGELOG, and raised as a User question.

decisions.choice: Derive the Producer and Verifier budgets from a stated rule: the smallest multiple of 50 that keeps the largest set at or below 90% (the producer set, or the planner against Producer; the verifier set, or the critic against Verifier), provided the pin in run_pin_tests.rs:1607-1618 still holds (contract + 2 verifier frames exceeds the Verifier budget). Let C be the contract, V the verifier frame and K the largest capability verifier section, in tokens. The pin needs C+2V > B and the 90% rule needs C+V+K ≤ 0.9B, so both hold only while 0.1·C + K < 0.8·V, before the 50-step rounding adds up to 49 to B. The producer checks this before writing the files and sets the byte targets with margin: contract about 830 bytes (C≈277), study verifier section about 800 bytes (K≈267), verifier frame about 1300 bytes (V≈433). That gives a set of about 977 and a Verifier budget of 1100 (89%). The pin sum is about 1143, a margin of about 43 tokens, and the inequality margin is about 51. Producer set about 927 gives 1050 (88%). All are estimates from byte targets; the producer takes the final numbers from the budgets test output. Each constant gets a comment that states the rule by relation (largest set, 90%, context-engineer.md §8) and the inequality, with no measured figure. Contract (350) and Reader (2000) stay; no budget rises.
decisions.reason: context-engineer.md §8 (229-237) says a set above 95% must name what it removes and Hestia flags sets above 90%. A fixed '+50' rule starts the sets near 97%. The inequality turns the interaction with the pin into a check the producer can do first. Trimming V cuts the pin side by 2 tokens for every 1 token off the real set, so it breaks the pin first; the plan therefore lengthens V's margin and trims K or C instead. Contract and Reader are pinned by literals in run_pin_tests.rs:1625 ('of 2000 tokens') and live.rs:249-252 (350). Neither file is a deliverable, so their extra headroom is stated, not cut.

rejected.why: Wrong direction: it lowers the pin side twice as fast as the set. Fallback is now: shrink the study verifier section or the contract, or keep V longer.

risks.risk: A rewrite drops a phrase a test pins, or states something a verdict rule forbids; check_verifier_prompt splits clauses on commas and full stops, so an innocent sentence can match a forbidden pattern.
risks.mitigation: Keep the anchor list verbatim (lib.rs:441-543, briefs.rs:1585-1616, verify.rs REQUIRED_FIELDS, the cap-change fragment). After each prompt file run cargo test -p athena-context and cargo test -p athena-core --lib verify; fix before the next file.

risks.risk: The 90% budget target and the run_pin_tests.rs:1618 pin (contract + 2 verifier frames above the Verifier budget) conflict. Trimming the verifier frame V makes this worse, because it lowers the pin side by 2 tokens per token cut and the real set by 1. Both hold only while 0.1·C + K < 0.8·V, and rounding B up to a multiple of 50 adds up to 49 tokens to the pin's burden.
risks.mitigation: Before writing files, compute the inequality from the byte targets (C≈277, K≈267, V≈433 give a margin of about 51 tokens). Step 5 measures the real sizes and checks the pin directly. If they conflict, shrink the study verifier section or the contract further, or lengthen the verifier frame; never trim VERIFIER_FRAME and never edit the pin test. If still unresolved, choose the smaller multiple of 50 (a set between 90% and 95%) and state the shortfall in the comment and CHANGELOG, per the User question.

risks.risk: On a repository other than Athena's, the pointer names a missing file and the agent loses the explanation the doc holds.
risks.mitigation: The pointer is conditional, only explanation and examples move, and every pinned or imperative rule and the severity definitions stay in the frame. The new test fails if an anchor is absent from a frame or present in the doc. The limit is stated in the doc header and the CHANGELOG, and the User question asks about compiling it in.

risks.risk: The anchor list in the new test is incomplete, so a rule could still migrate to the doc unnoticed.
risks.mitigation: The list is built from the criterion 6 anchors and the severity terms, and the producer must add any imperative sentence it considers moving. The doc header says it holds no rules. Criterion 3's diff review checks every deleted line.

risks.risk: In a study job only pinned-source/ is meant to be read, and the common frames now point at a doc.
risks.mitigation: The pointer is optional and the doc holds no study rules; the capability sections carry no pointer, which the new test asserts.

risks.risk: The new tracked doc trips the boundary scan or the personal-data allow-list.
risks.mitigation: Do not name the people or machines the scan lists; write no email-like text. Run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` after writing the doc.

risks.risk: The full suite takes 9 to 11 minutes and the last step may be skipped.
risks.mitigation: Run the targeted tests after each step and the full cargo test --locked once at the end.

risks.risk: The rewrite makes agents worse in ways a byte count cannot show.
risks.mitigation: Only restatements and explanation are removed; hard rules and severity definitions stay. The CHANGELOG states counts as estimates (⌈bytes/3⌉), not live measurements; quality shows only on later jobs.
